findings.title: totalPages off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages is computed as floor(user_count/limit)+1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 users, limit 50), this yields 2 pages instead of 1. The page indicator is then wrong, showingLast stays false on the real last page, and 'next' navigates to an empty page. Use Math.ceil(user_count/limit).

findings.title: create ignores alias_level
findings.body: The client sends alias_level in asJSON, but create only sets name and visible. Any alias level the admin picks when creating a group is silently discarded.

findings.title: Unbounded limit on public members endpoint
findings.body: limit comes straight from params with no cap. Any user who can see the group can request limit=1000000 and load every member in a single query. Negative values are also passed through unchecked. Clamp limit to a sane range, e.g. 1..200.

findings.title: Stale pagination offset when revisiting a group
findings.body: Group models are cached in the adminGroups list, so offset persists between visits. Returning to a group can show a later page rather than page 1. findMembers also clamps offset against the old user_count, which may be out of date.

findings.title: automatic not resolvable in item view context
findings.body: Inside the `each ... itemView` item view, `automatic` is looked up on the item context rather than the group. It may be undefined, so remove links can appear for automatic groups. Clicking one fails with a 422 from the server.

findings.title: remove_member automatic test uses wrong verb
findings.body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test sends PUT, but the route for remove_member is DELETE. The test therefore does not exercise the actual routed request.

findings.title: No error handling for add/remove member
findings.body: The promises returned by addMembers and removeMember have no rejection handler. A failure such as a 422 is not reported to the admin, and the usernames input is never cleared after a successful add.
